transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi… thanks. I guess what finally made me come in is, um, it’s a small thing maybe, but I keep noticing I can’t seem to stay seated in certain meetings. Like during sprint planning at work, or even on mortgage calls, I know I should just sit there and focus, but I’ll suddenly get up to get water or decide I need to check something in the other room.

It’s not like I’m trying to be rude or avoid things, I just… do it before I’ve really thought it through. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been happening enough that I thought maybe I should ask someone.
Did you have similar trouble staying seated when you were a child, like in school or at home?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I was a good student, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was constantly in trouble or anything. But I do remember in elementary school teachers sometimes moving my desk closer to them, or reminding me to sit back down.

I’d pop up for things, or start talking before I was actually called on. And I think I had a habit of rushing through work even when I understood it. It wasn’t meant badly… I just had a hard time waiting, I guess. Does that count as the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high, energized, or irritable compared with your usual self?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a way that seems really out of character or like a clear “period,” if that makes sense.

I can get energized or irritated sometimes, sure, but it feels pretty tied to normal life stuff. I haven’t noticed anything where I felt unusually high or like a totally different version of myself. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
When you get up in those meetings, is it usually because you feel anxious or like something bad might happen if you don’t?

No, I don’t think it’s usually anxiety like that. I’m not sitting there thinking something bad will happen if I don’t get up.

It’s more like… I suddenly feel like I need water, or I remember something in the other room, and I’m already standing before I’ve really decided to. It sounds kind of silly when I say it, but that’s the thing that finally pushed me to come in, because it keeps happening during sprint planning or mortgage calls when I know I should just stay put.
Before you get up in those meetings, do you ever have a repeated unwanted thought that you need to act on?

I don’t think so… not like an unwanted thought that repeats or that I feel I have to obey.

It’s more just a quick impulse, I guess. Like the idea pops in and I’m moving before I’ve really paused to think about it. But I’m not having a specific scary or intrusive thought beforehand, if that’s what you mean. Does that answer it?
Does this tendency to act before thinking also happen in other parts of your life, not just during meetings?

Yeah… I think it does, a little. Not in a dramatic way, I hope, but I do catch myself answering teammates before they’ve finished explaining a bug or even finishing their question.

And then sometimes, as I’m already talking, I realize I guessed wrong about where they were going. Which is embarrassing, because I don’t mean to interrupt or come off like I’m not listening. I’m trying to be helpful, but… yeah, I guess that is another place it happens.
Have these impulsive moments caused problems for you at work, at home, or in relationships?

A little, yeah. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has started creating some friction.

At work, people have had to follow up with me more than they used to, especially around planning things, and I hate that because I really am trying. And at home too, there are times where I’ve acted too quickly or missed part of what someone was asking, and then it turns into this extra back-and-forth.

I guess I’m worried I’m starting to seem like the unreliable one with planning tasks, which… feels pretty awful to admit. Is that the kind of problem you mean?
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations, even when you want to pay attention?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I do want to pay attention, it’s not that I don’t care.

Like, I’ll sit down to review a pull request, or even read something important like mortgage documents, and I start with good intentions. But after a few minutes I’ll realize I’m just staring at the same section and my mind is off thinking about five unrelated things.

It’s a little embarrassing, because I should be able to just… read the thing. But yeah, that does happen. Is that what you mean by trouble staying focused?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping track of what needs to get done?

Yeah… I do, though I try to have systems for it, so it’s not like I’m totally dropping everything.

But honestly, my work tickets, home repair notes, budget reminders… they end up scattered all over the place — Slack messages, sticky notes, email, my phone. And then I spend this ridiculous amount of time trying to figure out what I was supposed to do next instead of just doing it.

It sounds kind of minor when I say it out loud, but it does slow me down. Is that the kind of organization trouble you mean?
Do you ever get repeated unwanted thoughts that feel intrusive and hard to dismiss?

Um… not really, I don’t think so.

I mean, I get worries stuck in my head sometimes, like replaying whether I handled something correctly, but I wouldn’t say they feel intrusive in the way you’re describing. Not like unwanted thoughts I can’t dismiss, at least not that I’ve noticed.

If there’s a specific kind of thought you mean, I can try to think about it more.
